title: Computational and experimental assessment of key interdomain residues controlling the fold-switch of RfaH.
authors: Tabilo-Agurto, Cyndi; Reyes, Javiera; Artsimovitch, Irina; Ramirez-Sarmiento, Cesar A
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
one_liner_zh: 该文结合MD模拟、AlphaFold2结构预测与体内实验，评估RfaH转录因子CTD结构域折叠转换的关键残基，虽聚焦蛋白构象变化而非直接TF-DNA结合界面，但涉及转录因子调控机制且方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模。
abstract: Escherichia coli RfaH, a member of the universally conserved NusG family of transcription factors, regulates its function by undergoing a structural rearrangement of its C-terminal domain (CTD) upon recruitment to RNA polymerase (RNAP) paused at the DNA signal known as operon polarity suppressor (ops) element. While it is known that the fold-switch of RfaH CTD from an alpha-helical hairpin (autoinhibited state) into a beta-barrel (active state) is controlled by interactions between the N-terminal domain (NTD) and CTD, which are broken apart upon NTD binding to RNAP, a comprehensive analysis of residues that stabilize the autoinhibited state is lacking. Here, we utilize a combination of molecular dynamics (MD), protein structure prediction, and in vivo functional assays as a workflow to determine key interdomain (ID) residues controlling the fold-switch of RfaH. First, MD simulations employing structure-based models identified eight CTD residues with high ID contact probability, therefore expected to play a crucial role in stabilizing the autoinhibited state of RfaH. In silico alanine scanning mutagenesis followed by structure prediction using AlphaFold2 showed that four of these mutants (F126A, E136A, R138A, and L142A) led to several models with mixed alpha/beta secondary structure for the CTD in comparison to the known fold-switching mutant E48A. Lastly, experimental alanine scanning mutagenesis and RfaH-dependent in vivo luminescence assays confirmed that I129 and L142 contribute to the stabilization of the autoinhibited state. These results deepen our understanding of the fold-switch of RfaH, with tools that are applicable to other metamorphic proteins.
abstract_zh: 大肠杆菌RfaH，作为普遍保守的NusG转录因子家族成员，通过在其被招募至停滞于DNA信号（称为操纵子极性抑制子（operon polarity suppressor, ops）元件）的RNA聚合酶（RNAP）时，其C端结构域（CTD）发生结构重排来调节其功能。尽管已知RfaH CTD从α-螺旋发夹（自抑制状态）转变为β-桶状（活性状态）的折叠转换受N端结构域（NTD）与CTD之间相互作用的控制，这些相互作用在NTD结合RNAP时被破坏，但缺乏对稳定自抑制状态残基的全面分析。在此，我们利用分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）、蛋白质结构预测和体内功能检测相结合的工作流程，来确定控制RfaH折叠转换的关键结构域间（ID）残基。首先，采用基于结构模型的MD模拟识别出八个具有高ID接触概率的CTD残基，因此预期它们在稳定RfaH自抑制状态中发挥关键作用。通过计算机模拟丙氨酸扫描诱变，随后使用AlphaFold2进行结构预测，结果显示，与已知的折叠转换突变体E48A相比，其中四个突变体（F126A、E136A、R138A和L142A）导致CTD出现多种混合α/β二级结构的模型。最后，实验性丙氨酸扫描诱变和RfaH依赖性体内发光检测证实，I129和L142有助于稳定自抑制状态。这些结果加深了我们对RfaH折叠转换的理解，所采用的方法也适用于其他变形蛋白。
